gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-vend-sans: Vend Sans draws its lines like a ruler, with wide-open curve endings. Nulshock stretches out above it, bold and technical, so a long page of text would feel crisp and unhurried.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-yaldevi: Nulshock's stretched, widely tracked capitals sit barely taller than its lowercase, all in a steady outline. Yaldevi's oversized lowercase and open sans e answer it.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-orbit: Orbit is a sans-serif whose curves stop short of closing and whose characters float apart from each other. And Oldtimer's round, parenthesis-like forms give it a commanding heading, while a long stretch of Orbit reads smooth as rope.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-science-gothic: Oldtimer's round forms look like open parentheses, with no calligraphic swell on any downstroke. Science Gothic follows as a plain sans, its far-apart stroke ends making you take each letter one at a time.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-syncopate: Round, classic, commanding up top. Syncopate underneath is a plain sans with open shapes and technical-pen steadiness, and that stark gap between the two is where this pairing gets its pull.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-abeezee: ABeeZee reads like neon glass tubing, with terminals that finish well clear of the stem and a high mean line. And Origami's single-stroke brush look and leaden lowercase keep a long page lively without tiring the eye.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-aldrich: Aldrich is a sans-serif with an x-height close to its caps and cupped, unclenched round letters. Aldrich against Origami's brushed, lead-heavy lowercase gives the pair its strongest quality: a sharp split between handmade and modern.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-alexandria: Unique is the mood of Origami, whose single-stroke, one-tip simplicity makes every glyph look drawn in one go. Alexandria's tall, sans-serif body with open terminals steadies it.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-amiko: Modern in feel, Amiko is a sans-serif with outward-pointing terminals, set under Origami's crossbars, which are as fat as its stems. Longer text stays brisk and easy.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-anek-bangla: Anek Bangla reads wide and friendly, its s curves barely curled in and its ascenders kept short. But Origami's heading has no swelling where curves meet stems, and that smooth, brush-like sameness is the strongest thing here.
